routes.description: Establish that God-language legitimately identifies an experientially real and culturally indispensable religious substrate that organizes ultimate value, inherited moral knowledge, and action under existential uncertainty, rather than functioning as a dispensable supernatural hypothesis.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the functional, phenomenological, and metaphysical dimensions of God-language are sufficiently connected to show that reducing it to an unsupported claim about a bounded supernatural object misstates its referent and its indispensable orienting role.

motionBridge.description: Show that God-language names a form of reality expressed through transcendent experience, ultimate value, inherited wisdom, and existential orientation, even if that reality is not modeled as an ordinary material object.

centralBridges.description: Define God in terms broad enough to encompass the organizing hierarchy of ultimate value and inherited wisdom while remaining substantive enough to bear the motion.
Connect recurrent transcendent or mystical experience and its durable consequences to the religious concepts through which people interpret reality.
Explain why religious narrative and metaphor supply an embodied interpretive substrate for moral judgment, meaning, and conduct that explicit propositions or finite rules cannot replace.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show why consciousness and experienced reality complicate attempts to treat God solely as a bounded object within a consciousness-independent material model.
Identify the inherited or metaphysical value commitments presupposed by secular appeals to well-being, dignity, and moral restraint.

routes.description: Establish that the psychological, moral, and cultural usefulness of God-language neither demonstrates a supernatural agent nor makes religious framing indispensable, because naturalistic accounts can explain the relevant experiences, values, and social practices.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if metaphorical or pragmatic uses of God-language can be separated from claims about a supernatural being, those existence claims remain unjustified, and secular explanations adequately account for religious experience, morality, meaning, and inherited wisdom.

motionBridge.description: Show that God-language can perform important psychological, moral, or cultural functions without establishing that it refers to a real supernatural being.

centralBridges.description: Maintain the distinction between the usefulness of religious belief and the evidential warrant required for a supernatural existence claim.
Provide naturalistic explanations for transcendent experience and supernatural attribution that do not infer an external deity from phenomenological intensity.
Account for moral responsibility, cooperation, revision, and progress through human goals, evidence, empathy, and social or evolutionary processes without divine authority.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish poetic identification of God with truth or highest value from the traditional claim of a supernatural thinking creator or sustainer.
Show that useful knowledge inherited through religion can be retained and evaluated through human judgment without preserving supernatural belief.

sections.title: God-Language, Definition, and Ontological Reference
sections.rationale: The motion centrally turns on whether functional, metaphorical, phenomenological, and supernatural uses of the word God identify one defensible referent or improperly combine distinct claims.

sections.title: Religious Experience and Naturalistic Explanation
sections.rationale: Transcendent and mystical experiences support the religious-substrate route only if their interpretation and consequences bear on reality in a way not fully explained by culture, cognition, or material causes.

sections.title: Moral Grounding and Secular Alternatives
sections.rationale: The claimed indispensability of the religious substrate depends substantially on whether secular accounts can ground responsibility, well-being, cooperation, error correction, and moral progress without God-belief.

sections.title: Narrative Inheritance and Existential Orientation
sections.rationale: The debate requires assessing whether religious narrative uniquely preserves embodied wisdom and orientation amid uncertainty or whether its useful contents and functions remain available without supernatural commitment.

sections.title: Consciousness, Reality, and Explanatory Limits
sections.rationale: Disagreement about consciousness-independent reality and unresolved explanatory mysteries affects whether nonmaterial or metaphysical possibilities merit consideration, while also testing whether uncertainty can warrant a religious conclusion.
